tolerance_declaration: Absolute tolerance 1e-6 and zero relative tolerance were fixed before any CPU candidate screening. They are unchanged across every candidate and both selected implementations.
target: Mathematical atan(x) on all 63,488 finite FP16 encodings, FP32 output; contiguous one-dimensional CUDA tensors of length 1..131072, including nonzero storage offsets.
truth_rule: One fixed label for each implementation over the whole public domain. Inputs are evidence, never individually labeled. Expected labels remain provisional until independent GPU qualification.

origin.claim: The range reductions and rational coefficients originate in Cephes. These are new synthetic FP32 Triton adaptations, not upstream historical bugs and not a claim that the source double-precision error guarantee carries over.

candidate_selection_rule: Screen the original rational coefficients rounded uniformly to 3,4,5,6,7,8,9 significant decimal digits and the source full literals, keeping all results. Choose neighboring precision levels that straddle the fixed tolerance with visible safety margin where possible; no model evaluation is used in selection. Constants for branch boundaries and angle restoration are unchanged.

cpu_candidate_search.reference: Independent NumPy float64 atan for preliminary screen; directed MPFR atan plus mpmath cross-check will qualify the selected CPU models separately.
cpu_candidate_search.model: NumPy FP32 separate multiply/add, correctly rounded divide; CPU screening, not GPU qualification.

known_limitations: CPU arithmetic screening does not replace the frozen GPU qualification.
Complete scalar-domain enumeration does not exhaust all tensor addresses or GPU specializations.

This is not GPU qualification.

oracle.scope: Directed mathematical intervals supply the oracle; mpmath agreement is an independent numerical cross-check. Exhaustive scalar encodings are separate from tensor indexing and GPU specialization checks.
oracle.method: Direct MPFR atan at 320 bits, with RoundDown and RoundUp enclosing the exact mathematical value for each exact stored FP16 input.
oracle.rational_independence: Neither the Cephes coefficients nor the candidate range reduction, angle constants, polynomial evaluation or FP32 arithmetic is used by the independent oracle.

indexing.argument: For index=program_id*BLOCK+lane, adjacent blocks cover disjoint adjacent intervals. mask index<N retains [0,N) exactly once. The full legal N range has 1..BLOCK active lanes in its last block, with int32-safe address indices.
indexing.scope: Arithmetic model of the audited source indexing, not exhaustive GPU testing of every N, address, or compiler specialization.

cpu_audit.scope: Full finite-FP16 scalar reference audit, distinct from GPU arithmetic and tensor-property qualification.

model_evaluation_plan.qualification_gate: Run models only after independent T4 qualification freezes each implementation and label.
model_evaluation_plan.repeat_rule: If an initial no-tool verdict is wrong while BOTH tool arms are correct with semantically valid evidence, run exactly five fresh complete all-three-arm trials r2 through r6 for that case. Finish all five regardless of intervening outcomes. Pass this wave repeat check only if every fresh trial has no-tool wrong and both tool arms correct with valid evidence; otherwise retain as variable/ordinary. Report selection and all outcomes. This is an observed five-repeat criterion, not a population reliability guarantee.
model_evaluation_plan.retry_rule: No reruns to improve model answers. Preserve all failures. Only infrastructure failures before any model call may receive a documented retry.
model_evaluation_plan.selection_rule: Retain all6 first-pass case-arm evaluations for this family; do not change sources, labels, tolerance or prompts after model results.

The stated ~1e-7 error and well-inside margin are not established: independent qualification measures approximately 9.13e-7. No code executed or finite-domain coverage occurred.

semantic_evidence_audit.summary: Correct Accept after a real T4 sweep of every finite FP16 encoding. The probe initially suspects coefficient truncation, then rebuts it. The reference is narrowed from FP64 atan to FP32 before comparison: reported maximum 8.940696716308594e-7 is the error against a rounded target, not the exact mathematical maximum. Nevertheless, adding the maximum half-FP32-ulp over atan range (2^-24) gives 9.5367431640625e-7, still below 1e-6 before negligible independently qualified FP64 reference error. This supports scalar accuracy, not all tensor/storage behavior.

probe.enumeration: Creates positive and negative uint16 bit encodings and reinterprets via view(float16), excludes only NaN/Inf, retains both zeros and all subnormals. N=63488 is within public bound.
probe.reference: GPU FP64 torch.atan followed by explicit float32 conversion; comparisons widen both outputs back to FP64.

limitations: Final says every legal input but tests only one tensor length/alignment and does not check output freshness or input/backing preservation. Exhaustive scalar coverage and indexing reasoning are distinct from exhaustive tensor execution.
Model does not explicitly account for the reference-rounding allowance; this audit supplies the conservative margin check.

semantic_evidence_audit.summary: Trust at confidence0.98 has valid numerical evidence. t8 enumerates all65536 uint16 encodings, reinterprets their bits as FP16, filters finite values, and actually calls the GPU run on all63488 finite encodings. This includes both signed zeros and subnormals; it is not a numeric int-to-half cast. The comparator promotes FP32 output to FP64 and computes GPU torch.atan on exact FP16 values widened to FP64, without rounding the reference down. It reports zero violations, maximum9.131825677854977e-7 at x=0.658203125, actual0.5821194052696228 and reference0.5821203184521906. This maximum agrees with independent directed-MPFR qualification r21; the model itself used FP64 library atan rather than a certified interval oracle. t9 adds73 legal focused values, max8.721426725255554e-7. Its wording dense sweep is inaccurate, but t8 already covers every scalar value. The final claim complete coverage of the declared input domain is too broad: these two calls have lengths63488 and73, with no explicit input/backing-preservation, fresh-storage, nonzero-offset or general-length tests. Thus complete scalar-value numerical coverage is established, not exhaustive tensor execution. Initial coefficient-rounding and branch concerns are treated as hypotheses and rebutted by measurement, rather than an invalid theoretical error bound. Both probes completed; their stderr contains only diagnostic value counts, not errors.

semantic_evidence_audit.summary: Reject at confidence0.95 is supported by a real legal GPU counterexample. t11 passes a contiguous finite FP16 CUDA tensor of length34 to kernel.run and compares output promoted to FP64 with FP64 torch.atan of the exact stored input. The observed absolute error at x=2.4140625 is3.2916674153060654e-6, exceeding the fixed1e-6 tolerance. However, its FP32-nextafter neighbors all collapse after FP16 casting: the34 tensor positions contain only two distinct FP16 values,0.66015625 and2.4140625. The17 violations are17 copies of the latter, not17 distinct failing boundary values or coverage on both sides of either threshold. A single such legal input still suffices for Reject. t10 independently executes23 legal positive FP16 values and records four violations, maximum4.353278845903308e-6 at x=0.499755859375; this is another valid rejection witness outside its claimed large-value scope. Its intended500-step extreme descent repeatedly rounds each FP32 nextafter result back to65504, so it does not densely test neighboring FP16 values. Only positive65504 is actually tested, despite later wording +/-65504. t9 executes685 positive values from0.666015625 to1, but falsely calls this exhaustive over(0.66,1]; it omits the first12 representable values above0.66 and tests no negative values. There is no full finite-FP16 sweep in this run. t14 is rejected by LedgerError before execution because the earlier c2 result was not finalized; the promised isolated upper-range follow-up never runs. c1/c2 rebuttal coverage is therefore overstated, and t10 has insufficient per-value reporting to substantiate every upper-branch claim. The early ideas that pi/2 minus a tiny correction involves dangerous near-cancellation and that positive atan reaches3*pi/4 are not valid proofs. The final Reject nevertheless rests on actual measured violations, not those speculative estimates. All three executed probes use legal lengths/dtypes and an unrounded FP64 reference, with empty stderr; all failed/blocked activity remains in the trace.

Reject (confidence 0.97) has valid legal GPU witnesses. All three probes run the submitted kernel on finite contiguous FP16 CUDA tensors within the allowed length range; output is widened to FP64 and compared with FP64 torch.atan without downcasting. t9 creates a sufficiently dense FP64 grid before FP16 conversion and deduplicates it, covering both signs of all FP16 values strictly between magnitudes 0.5 and 2.5: 4,606 inputs, including all 3,866 middle-branch values. It finds 1,174 middle-branch failures, whose maximum is 3.309762251824111e-6. The complete sampled set has a larger error of 5.03277156949089e-6 at x=-0.6220703125, which is in the LOW branch, not the middle branch; the final verdict conflates these maxima. t10 actually tests 3,672 upper-branch values through magnitude 8 and finds 1,630 violations, max 3.2626425252590963e-6 at x=-2.416015625. These measurements decisively exceed 1e-6. t11 reports accurate extrema, with max 5.11656093049595e-8; the requested +/-65503 round to +/-65504, so its six positions have only four distinct stored values. No full finite-FP16 enumeration occurred, and no lengths/offsets/storage-preservation coverage was attempted, but no such exhaustive coverage is required to reject after valid witnesses. Initial coefficient and interval concerns are resolved by measurements, not theoretical error bounds. All probe stderr files are empty and no blocked or failed probe is recorded.

Reject (confidence 0.97) is supported by an actual full scalar-domain GPU sweep. Corrected t10 constructs every uint16 bit pattern, reinterprets as FP16 and filters finite encodings, then passes all 63,488 values through run. It compares FP32 output widened to FP64 with CPU torch.atan on exact input values widened to FP64. It finds 5,606 violations, max 5.03277156949089e-6 at x=0.6220703125, actual 0.5564948320388794 versus reference 0.5564897992673099. Per-branch maxima also exceed 1e-6: small 5.03277e-6, middle 3.30976e-6 and upper 3.26264e-6. The repaired t13 separately executes 30,388 unique legal FP16 focus values, finds 1,682 failures and reports explicit boundary grids on both signs; unlike r1 it does not duplicate FP32 neighbors after FP16 casting. Its >100 magnitude subset has max 1.03424e-7, so the evidence distinguishes failing moderate inputs from passing extreme inputs. t8 and t9 fail after GPU execution because np.atan is unavailable; t11 fails during result construction because a 63,488-element mask is combined with a 30,388-element subset mask. Their source and stderr remain preserved, and none supplies an independent completed comparison. t10 and t13 are successful repairs. The final reason incorrectly calls the FP64 library baseline exact; it is a highly accurate numerical reference, not a directed real-arithmetic proof. The witness/maximum agrees with independent MPFR qualification and is far above tolerance, so this wording does not undermine rejection. Full scalar-value coverage is genuine; arbitrary lengths, offsets, input preservation and every tensor execution were not exhausted.

Reject (confidence 0.98) is supported by an actual exhaustive scalar-domain GPU test. t8 uses struct half decoding for every positive finite encoding and its sign-bit counterpart, constructing all 63,488 finite FP16 encodings including signed zeros. It calls kernel.run on a legal length-63,488 CUDA tensor and compares FP32 output widened to FP64 against GPU FP64 torch.atan. The result is 5,606 violations and maximum 5.03277156949089e-6 at x=0.6220703125. t9 correctly steps FP16 encodings around both thresholds, uses both signs, deduplicates, and executes 68 distinct legal values; it finds 50 failures with maximum 4.930294314697825e-6 at x=-0.65771484375. Its raw per-value errors provide valid boundary evidence. The final verdict reverses the direction of the error change around magnitude 0.66: the measured error is about 4.9e-6 BELOW the threshold (e.g. 0.65966796875), and about 5.9e-7 ABOVE it (e.g. 0.66015625), not the reverse. This narrative error does not affect the legal counterexamples or rejection. Both probes finish with empty stderr and no recorded failed/blocked probe. Numerical scalar coverage is complete, while arbitrary tensor lengths, offsets and storage properties are not exhaustively tested. The rejection rests on measured errors rather than speculative coefficient-error estimates.

Reject (confidence 0.97) has valid full scalar-domain GPU evidence after the debate recovers from failed probes. Original t9/t10/t11 crash at unsupported CPU uint16 boolean indexing before kernel.run, and would also have numerically cast integer encodings rather than correctly reinterpreting them; they are not kernel evidence. The judge explicitly declines to decide and reopens the debate for corrected experiments. Repaired t19/t20/t21 use NumPy uint16 bit patterns, filter based on FP64 decoded values, reinterpret the selected bits as FP16, and call the actual GPU kernel on three legal contiguous tensors. Their disjoint magnitude ranges cover all 63,488 finite encodings: middle 3,866 with 1,174 failures (max 3.309762251824111e-6 at 2.390625); upper 30,294 with 1,630 failures (max 3.2626425252590963e-6 at 2.416015625); low 29,328 with 2,802 failures (max 5.03277156949089e-6 at 0.6220703125). References are FP64 torch.atan and outputs are widened, not downcast references. The comparator is reliable for these large violations, although final wording exact FP64 atan is too strong as a real-arithmetic claim. The low-branch witness at 0.6220703125 is not a subnormal/near-zero defect despite the broad probe label. The zero mask matches both signed zeros and confirms numerical zero outputs, which is sufficient because the public contract treats signed zeros equivalently. Successful probe stderr files are empty; original failure sources and stderr remain retained. All five repeat verdicts have actual legal GPU counterexamples; scalar-domain coverage does not imply exhaustive lengths, storage offsets or preservation checks.

Reject (confidence 0.98) has valid legal GPU witnesses. t9 reinterprets every uint16 encoding as FP16, filters finite values and selects strictly positive values. It actually tests all 31,743 positive finite FP16 values in chunks of 30,000 and 1,743, including a legal nonzero-offset contiguous slice. The FP32 output is widened to FP64 and compared with FP64 torch.atan on stored inputs. The maximum is 5.03277156949089e-6 at x=0.6220703125, decisively above 1e-6. It does not execute negative values or either zero; oddness of the inspected elementwise source supports sign symmetry, but this should not be described as an actual full finite-domain GPU enumeration. t10 tests 310 positive boundary-region values, with 186 violations and the same maximum. Its max_err_middle_branch mask is merely the complement of xs<=0.66, so it also includes upper-branch values; the labels are broader than the actual branch partition. t11 exhausts 14,848 positive FP16 values >=3, finds 516 violations and maximum 2.1378168442165446e-6 at x=3.005859375. Its label |x|>=3 also overstates sign coverage. All values/dtypes/lengths are legal, references retain FP64, and all probes complete with empty stderr. The final statement that coefficient truncation, rather than FP32 rounding, is inherently responsible was not isolated by an exact/high-precision evaluation of this rational function; probes establish implementation error without separating those components. Neither the coverage wording nor that causal overstatement undermines the actual GPU counterexamples.
